description: Micro-tune the n=512 B=640 dense two-level FP16 path (shape 3, the single heaviest benchmark shape at 3742us, plus rankdef shape9/clustered shape10). Sweep the outer/inner block sizes (QR_BIGBATCH_OB around 64, IB around 16), panel warp count (_BIGBATCH_WARPS=8), minv_nt, the wf16/inner_wmma/panel_apply_fused fusion flags, and ov_fold, profiling with ncu to find the occupancy/barrier-latency optimum. Goal: shave the SIMT-sgemm trailing time without changing the algorithm. Profile-grounded only; report which knob moved the needle.

Scaffolding: parameterize n=512 mixed-driver knobs via QR_N512_* env vars (qr_n512_mixed_driver + set_n512_good/indexed_flags now read g_n512_* statics; OB locked at 64 because fill_R_n512_ob64_ib16_* assumes 64x64 R blocks, IB/warps/minv_nt/paf_warps/ov_fold/fusion sweepable). Defaults reproduce parent exactly; geomean 2084.6us == baseline (noise). Enables zero-recompile sweeps.

Swept n=512 minv_nt 224->208 (isolated 3-shape-proxy optimum, ~0.25% reproducible over 2 runs; 192/216/240/256 worse). Also swept (all confirmed parent-optimal): paf_warps 8 (16 is +20%), IB 16 (8/24/32 far worse), paf_no_csh 1 (0 is +3.5%), ov_fold 1 (off +10%), wf16 1 (off +19%), inner_wmma 2 (1 asserts/unsupported), panel_defer locked at 5 (others TORCH_CHECK), minv_blk4 1, panel_cm 1, g_warps tied 4/8. Full geomean 2083.6us.

Brief exhausted. Best: geomean 2083.6us (HEAD 65b45da, minv_nt 224->208) vs 2081.5 baseline -- effectively FLAT (the n=512 path is only 3-4 of 12 shapes; a 0.25% per-shape proxy win washes into full-geomean noise). KEY FINDING: the brief's premise is stale -- there is NO custom SIMT-sgemm trailing GEMM; the simt_sgemm in the whole-bench profile is the CHECKER's householder_product. The custom n=512 trailing GEMMs are already nvjet TF32 tensor-op. The dominant custom kernel for shapes 3/9/10 is qr_panel_apply_fused_kernel (the PAF megakernel, ~52ms/630launches in nsys). WHAT WORKED: minv_nt=208 (marginal, reproducible isolated-only). WHAT DIDN'T (all parent values confirmed optimal): paf_warps must stay 8 (16=+20%, occupancy), IB must stay 16 (8/24/32 far worse, OB LOCKED at 64 by fill_R_n512_ob64_ib16_*), paf_no_csh=1 (0=+3.5%), ov_fold=1 (off=+10%), wf16=1 (off=+19%), inner_wmma forced 2 (1 asserts), panel_defer locked 5. I added QR_N512_* env knobs + g_n512_* statics so these are now zero-recompile sweepable. NCU on the PAF kernel: 50% THEORETICAL occupancy (smem-limited to 4 blocks/SM), latency-bound, ~5 cycles/warp stalled at CTA barriers (the warp-0 serial pivot chain). SUGGESTED NEXT DIRECTION (MACRO, off this brief): the only headroom is structural -- restructure the PAF kernel's warp-specialized pivot to 2-reflectors-per-barrier (like the small-n panel_cm2 path) to cut the barrier stall, OR shrink its smem footprint below the 4-block/SM ceiling to lift occupancy. Also the entry-time f32_to_bf16_kernel (whole B=640x512x512 H->bf16, DRAM-bound 72%, ~4.9ms) is a fusable HBM round-trip worth a structural brief.

Micro-tuning the n=512 B=640 path is exhausted (flat). Pursue the two STRUCTURAL wins you identified. PRIMARY: the entry f32_to_bf16_kernel converts the whole B=640x512x512 H tensor to bf16 in a separate DRAM-bound pass (~72% DRAM, ~4.9ms HBM round-trip) — fuse that conversion into the first consumer (the first panel-factor smem load / Gram read) so the FP32->bf16 cast happens on-chip during the load that already touches those bytes, eliminating the full round-trip. SECONDARY if time: restructure the qr_panel_apply_fused (PAF) megakernel's warp-0 serial pivot to 2-reflectors-per-barrier (mirror the small-n panel_cm2 path) to cut the ~5-cycle/warp CTA-barrier stall. Profile the PAF + conversion kernels in isolation.

Scaffolding for convert-fusion: added f32_to_bf16_colrange_kernel (+indexed variant) that convert only columns [c0,c1), and a side-stream overlap path in blocked_qr_2level_bf16_indexed gated by g_fuse_convert (QR_N512_FUSE_CONVERT, default 0). When on (n=512/OB=64): convert [0,OB) on the main stream, [OB,n) bulk on a non-blocking side stream that overlaps the ko=0 inner panels/applies (which read only [0,OB)); main stream waits on a side-stream event before the ko=0 outer apply. Default OFF reproduces parent exactly: geomean 2085.0us == 2084.7 baseline (noise). Enables zero-recompile A/B of the overlap.

Enabled convert-fusion overlap (default ON). REGRESSION: geomean 2097.4us vs 2085.0 parent (+0.6%). nsys (custom kernels, n512 isolation): the column-split convert (f32_to_bf16_colrange) is now 188us/repeat vs 163us for the single flat convert -- splitting [0,OB)/[OB,n) makes BOTH passes column-STRIDED (each row's span is contiguous but rows are gapped), degrading the coalesced bandwidth. AND the overlap does not materialize: the ko=0 PAF kernels launch 640 CTAs (~1.08 waves) that SATURATE all 148 SMs, leaving zero spare occupancy for the side-stream convert to run concurrently -- so it queues serially behind, paying the strided penalty with no hiding. Validation PASS (split convert is bit-identical). Conclusion: the n=512 B=640 path is occupancy-saturated; convert cannot be hidden behind compute. Reverting default to OFF next.

Reverted convert-fusion default to OFF: geomean 2088.8us == 2085.0/2084.7 parent (noise). CONVERT-FUSION CONCLUSION (PRIMARY target): the side-stream overlap cannot hide the FP32->BF16 convert because the n=512 B=640 path is occupancy-SATURATED (PAF launches 640 CTAs ~1.08 waves over 148 SMs), so a concurrent convert has no spare SMs and serializes; the column-split also makes the convert strided (188us vs 163us). The only way to truly eliminate the 163us convert on a saturated GPU is to FUSE the cast into an EXISTING read: the ko=0 outer-apply W=V^T C Gram (reads the [OB,n) bulk) would need a custom FP32-in batched WMMA GEMM with smem-blocked C-reuse -- high effort and unlikely to beat cuBLAS+convert (cuBLAS reads C once; a naive WMMA re-reads C wt=4x). The convert itself is already near-bandwidth-optimal standalone (163us for ~1GB ~= 6.4TB/s ~80% of peak). Scaffold (colrange kernels + side-stream path, flag default OFF) retained for the manager. Pivoting to SECONDARY: PAF barrier-stall restructure.

PAF SECONDARY attempt 1: register-cache warp-0's serial look-ahead (load next pivot column into reg[16] once, fuse reduce+update, drop the 2nd smem read) to shorten the critical path the bulk warps stall on at the CTA barrier. First cut (MR=16 unconditional) FAILED validation: the PAF kernel is ALSO the n=1024 path (m up to 1024), where MR=16 spans only 512 rows -> n=1024 cond2 8/8 wrong. Gated on m<=512 (n=1024 keeps the original two-pass loop): validation PASS. But REGRESSION: geomean 2147.6us vs 2085 parent (+3%); shape3 4216 vs 3748 (+12.5%). Root cause: REGISTER SPILL -- the PAF apply phase (WMMA fragments + S/M/W/Y smem pointers) already uses ~48 reg/thread near the limit; the 16-float cache spills to local memory, whose traffic is far worse than the smem re-read it replaced. My occupancy-headroom estimate was wrong (the apply phase, not the panel, sets the register pressure). Reverting. Conclusion: the PAF warp-0 barrier stall is NOT fixable via register-caching (no register headroom in this fused mega-kernel).

PAF SECONDARY attempt 2 (the brief's explicit directive): restructured the PAF panel phase to 2-reflectors-per-barrier (warp 0 looks ahead 2 columns factoring {i+2,i+3}; bulk applies the length-2 reflector block {i,i+1} to c>=i+4; ONE __syncthreads per 2 columns via paf_apply1/paf_factor helpers + a ping-pong sh_pair buffer to avoid the within-interval scalar race). Gated m<=512/even-w (n=1024 keeps single-step). Validation PASS (diff guard + invariance guard CLEAN -- numerically bit-identical, design is correct). But REGRESSION: geomean 2216.4us vs 2085 parent (+6.3%); shape3 4627 vs 3748 (+23%). Root cause: halving the barrier COUNT does not help because warp 0's serial look-ahead is the critical path -- the 2-reflector version DOUBLES warp 0's per-interval serial work (factor 2 cols sequentially, 4 applies + 2 norms, with inter-column RAW), so the barrier wait per interval ~doubles and the bulk (which finishes its 2 applies fast) waits longer on warp 0. This is exactly why the codebase already replaced the cm2 2-reflector small-n kernel with the register-cached 1-sync cmf_tmpl. CONCLUSION: the PAF barrier stall (ncu's 33-50% est) is NOT realizable -- it is an upper bound that mis-attributes warp-0's intrinsic serial look-ahead as removable barrier wait. Reverting.

Reverted both PAF barrier experiments -> parent-equivalent. Final brief-1 best = geomean 2083.2us (HEAD 0d9d371) == parent 2083.6 (FLAT). The convert-fusion scaffold (colrange kernels + side-stream path, QR_N512_FUSE_CONVERT default 0) is retained but inert. nsys profile of the n512 custom path saved under this commit. NET RESULT for brief-1: no profitable structural win found on either target -- both PRIMARY (convert fusion) and SECONDARY (PAF barrier) hit hard structural ceilings (documented in prior iteration rows).

Brief-1 (macro, both structural targets) EXHAUSTED with NO profitable win; best = parent (HEAD 0d9d371, 2083.2us == 2083.6 parent). Both targets hit hard structural ceilings, root-caused:

PRIMARY (fuse the 163us f32_to_bf16 convert): I built column-range convert kernels + a side-stream overlap (convert [0,OB) on main stream, [OB,n) bulk on a non-blocking side stream behind the ko=0 inner panels/applies, which read only [0,OB)). Validates bit-identically but REGRESSES to 2097us: the n=512 B=640 path is OCCUPANCY-SATURATED (PAF launches 640 CTAs ~1.08 waves over 148 SMs), so a concurrent convert has no spare SMs and serializes; the column split also makes the convert strided (188us vs 163us contiguous). The convert is already ~80% of HBM peak standalone. The ONLY way to truly eliminate it on a saturated GPU is to fuse the cast into an EXISTING read -- the ko=0 outer-apply W=V^T C Gram reads the [OB,n) bulk -- but that GEMM is cuBLAS BF16-tensor-core (FP32-in unsupported); a custom FP32-in WMMA GEMM would need smem-blocked C-reuse and is unlikely to beat cuBLAS+convert (cuBLAS reads C once; naive WMMA re-reads it). Scaffold retained, flag QR_N512_FUSE_CONVERT default OFF.

SECONDARY (PAF warp-0 serial pivot -> 2-reflectors-per-barrier): I tried BOTH (a) register-caching warp-0's look-ahead (REGRESSES 2148us: the PAF apply phase's WMMA fragments already pin registers near the limit, so the 16-float cache SPILLS to local memory -- worse than the smem re-read), and (b) the brief's exact 2-reflector-per-barrier restructure (VALIDATES bit-identical via paf_apply1/paf_factor helpers + ping-pong scalar buffer, but REGRESSES 2216us/+23% on shape3). Root cause of (b): halving the barrier COUNT doesn't help because warp-0's serial look-ahead IS the critical path -- 2-reflector DOUBLES warp-0's per-interval serial work (factor 2 cols with inter-column RAW), so each barrier wait ~doubles. This is exactly why the codebase already replaced its cm2 2-reflector small-n kernel with the register-cached 1-sync cmf_tmpl. ncu's 33-50% barrier-stall 'est local speedup' is an UPPER BOUND that mis-attributes warp-0's intrinsic serial dependency as removable.

SUGGESTED NEXT DIRECTIONS (off this brief): (1) The remaining PAF headroom per ncu is OCCUPANCY (smem-limited to 4 blocks/SM = 50% theoretical) and the TAIL (1.08 waves) -- both want a SMALLER PAF smem footprint to fit 5+ blocks/SM, NOT a barrier change. The biggest smem term is Vsh (m*w bf16, 16KB at m=512) + the apply pool; shrinking either lifts occupancy and shortens the tail. (2) The PAF warp-0 serial pivot could be PARALLELIZED across more warps (cooperative pivot, like the wsp_cm_coop path) instead of restructured -- spread the look-ahead m-passes over 2-4 warps so warp-0 isn't the lone critical path; this attacks the real bottleneck (warp-0 serial latency) rather than the barrier symptom. (3) The n=512 path is genuinely at its structural frontier on this hardware; further wins likely require an entirely different factorization (e.g. CholeskyQR2 at n=512 -- though W0 found it stalled/regressed at n512/n1024).

Your entry-fusion + 2-reflector tries regressed - and your fusion used a side STREAM which is BANNED by the remote harness (rejects cudaStream/getCurrentCUDAStream; local validate misses it - do NOT use streams). Parent reset to your legal 65b45dac. Pursue the REAL PAF headroom you identified: PAF is smem-limited to 4 blocks/SM (50% theoretical occupancy) + a 1.08-wave tail. CUT the PAF kernel's shared-memory footprint - the biggest term is Vsh = m*w bf16 (~16KB at m=512). Stage V in registers or tiles, or shrink the smem C/W staging, to fit 5+ blocks/SM and hide the warp-0 barrier latency. This attacks occupancy (the real limiter) not barrier count. Single-CTA, no streams. Profile shape 3 PAF occupancy (ncu achieved_occupancy / blocks-per-SM) before/after. Keep gates.

PAF occupancy attempt 1: store the panel scratch s[w*LDM] as HALF instead of FP32 (the panel pool is the DOMINANT smem term -- 32KB FP32 at m=512, BIGGER than Vsh's 16KB -- and it overlays the apply pool ~13.5KB in a disjoint phase, so halving it cuts PEAK smem 48.1->32.1KB, lifting smem-allowed occupancy 4->6 blocks/SM, capped to 5 by the 48-reg limit). All Householder reductions stay FP32-in-registers; only the smem column entries narrow to half (pst_ld/pst_st helpers, templated PST param, g_n512_paf_half_panel flag). Built OK. But VALIDATION FAILED (diff_correctness_guard): the standard test shapes + dense/cond2 benchmark shapes PASS, but CLUSTERED n=512 inputs lose orthogonality catastrophically (residual=0.33 vs allowed=0.0061, 5400x over) and nearrank marginally (0.008 vs 0.0061, 132x). Root cause: clustered inputs have near-collinear columns where the Householder reflector vectors need FULL FP32 in the panel scratch -- half's 10-bit mantissa rounds the in-place rank-1 trailing updates (colc[r]-=twinv*colj[r]) compounding over 16 columns, destroying the V orthogonality the apply then propagates. NOT fixable by FP32-diagonal tweak (error is 5000x, not marginal). Half panel storage is fundamentally too lossy for the worst-conditioned n=512 path.
